corrections.mechanism: Entity-controlled high-rate writes -> one DynamoDB partition for every bucket of that entity; invariant: bucket writes must spread across independently shardable partition keys before the per-partition WCU ceiling is reached.
notes_append: The Claude-coauthored root commit creates entity-keyed DynamoDB buckets and is contained in vulnerable v0.10.0.
The former 3902c8c2 -> 94a129ae edge was insufficient: 94a only migrates keys and injects metadata; it contains no shard selection, retry, or shard-count doubling.

The six-member atomic closure ends at 9f66c42f, which adds random shard selection, cross-shard retry, and conditional doubling after WCU exhaustion; 20 targeted async/sync tests pass at that exact commit.

The first-party advisory identifies <=0.10.0 as vulnerable and 0.10.1 as patched; v0.10.1 is the official merge carrier 481ce44d. Later aggregator commits improve proactive behavior but are not required for the client-side minimum security closure.

corrections.mechanism: A stable lexical workspace alias is hashed directly into the per-project memory namespace, so repointing that alias under a shared HOME reuses another real workspace's MEMORY.md; invariant: project-memory identity must bind to the canonical real workspace with a domain-separated, full-length key.
notes_append: The Claude-coauthored bce0d2ba delta adds initProjectMemory and keys its directory with sha256(literal workspacePath)[0:12]; the commit is exactly tag v0.4.0, and its parent has no per-project memory implementation.

First-party issue #46 identifies bce0d2ba/v0.4.0 as affected and demonstrates cross-workspace memory disclosure through a repointed lexical symlink. The published, unwithdrawn global GHSA formally aliases CVE-2026-14611 and cites the same issue, PR, and fix.

PR #49 is a squash. Its first member c6daf910 is the minimum semantic fix: canonical realpath plus a schema-separated full SHA-256 key. The second member only migrates legacy directories; the isolated c6daf910 tree passes its symlink-isolation test.

No fixed release tag exists in the repository. The global unreviewed advisory simultaneously says v0.4.0 is affected and that upgrading to v0.4.0 fixes it, so that sentence is rejected as contradictory metadata; this row claims a released vulnerable AI origin and commit-level fix, not a released fix version.
